stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Ornithologists comparing recordings made in 1985 and 2022 have found that song sparrows nesting beside a busy highway corridor in central Ohio no longer sound quite like their rural relatives. Exposed for nearly four decades to the low rumble of passing trucks and cars, ______. The researchers suspect that the higher notes carry more clearly over the traffic noise and so reach rivals and potential mates.
choices: the songs of these roadside sparrows have shifted upward in minimum pitch by several hundred hertz
these roadside sparrows now sing songs whose minimum pitch is several hundred hertz higher
an upward shift of several hundred hertz has occurred in the minimum pitch of these birds' songs
the minimum pitch of these roadside sparrows' songs has risen by several hundred hertz since then
explanation: Ask who was exposed for nearly four decades to traffic noise: the sparrows. The opening phrase has no subject of its own, so the first noun after the comma has to be the sparrows. Choice B starts with "these roadside sparrows," so the modifier attaches to the right noun.

A.why: You let the phrase "of these roadside sparrows" convince you that the birds come first. The first noun is actually "songs," so the sentence says the songs were exposed to traffic for decades. It was the birds that lived beside the highway.

C.why: You chose a sentence that sounds formal and complete. But its first noun is "an upward shift," which means the shift itself was exposed to traffic. A change in pitch can't be exposed to anything. Only the sparrows can.

D.why: You picked up on "sparrows" inside the phrase, but here it is only a possessive. The grammatical subject is "the minimum pitch," a property of the songs. That makes the pitch the thing that was exposed, when it should be the birds.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Many of the pigments that give vegetables their color dissolve in fat rather than in water, and this chemical detail has practical consequences for how those pigments reach the body. Absorbed far more efficiently when eaten alongside a source of dietary fat, ______. For this reason, some nutrition researchers suggest dressing raw carrot salads with a small amount of olive oil instead of serving them plain.
choices: carrots deliver more of their orange pigment, beta-carotene, to the bloodstream when paired with oil
people who add oil to carrots take up more of the orange pigment beta-carotene into their blood
beta-carotene, the orange pigment in carrots, reaches the bloodstream in larger amounts with oil
the bloodstream receives more beta-carotene, the orange pigment in carrots, when oil is present
explanation: The thing absorbed more efficiently is the pigment, not the vegetable, the eater, or the bloodstream. Choice C puts "beta-carotene" directly after the comma, so the opening modifier describes the right noun.

A.why: You chose the object that contains the pigment. The passage is about pigments being absorbed, and carrots are not absorbed into the body. Their beta-carotene is.

B.why: You chose the people affected rather than the substance described. The sentence would then say people are absorbed far more efficiently when eaten, which makes no sense.

D.why: You chose the place where absorption ends up. The bloodstream receives the pigment, but the bloodstream is not what gets absorbed. The pigment is.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Economists analyzing payroll records from 2012 to 2022 tracked how earnings changed for employees who voluntarily left one job for another. Compared with workers who stayed with a single employer over the same decade, ______. The gap was widest among employees under thirty, a pattern the authors attribute to younger workers' greater willingness to negotiate when changing positions.
choices: the wages of job switchers grew roughly twice as fast over the ten-year period
wage growth for job switchers was roughly twice as fast over the ten-year period
job switchers seeing their wages grow roughly twice as fast over the ten-year period
job switchers saw their wages grow roughly twice as fast over the ten-year period
explanation: The opening phrase compares one group of workers with another, so the subject after the comma has to be workers, "job switchers." That narrows the choices to C and D. Then check the verb. Choice D has a finite main verb, "saw," so the sentence is complete.

A.why: You compared unlike things. With "the wages" as the subject, the sentence compares job switchers' wages with workers who stayed. You need to compare workers with workers.

B.why: You compared a rate with people. "Wage growth" is a property of the switchers, not the switchers themselves, so the opening phrase is left without the noun it describes.

C.why: You found the right subject but stopped checking there. "Seeing" is a nonfinite -ing form, so "job switchers" never gets a main verb and the sentence is a fragment.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: When quarry workers broke through a layer of hardened volcanic ash, they exposed something paleobotanists rarely see: an entire forest from the coal age, buried in a single eruption. Preserved beneath the ash for nearly 300 million years, ______. That level of detail is allowing researchers to map which plant species grew beside one another, tree by tree, across several hectares.
choices: the paleobotanists excavating the site have found trees with leaves still attached
the trees at the site still bear their leaves and cones in their original positions
the excavation has revealed trees with leaves and cones in their original positions
the quarry's ash layer holds trees whose leaves and cones are in their original places
explanation: What sat beneath the ash for 300 million years? The ancient trees. Choice B begins with "the trees at the site," so the opening modifier attaches to the thing that was actually preserved.

A.why: You chose the people acting instead of the thing described. The sentence would say the paleobotanists were preserved beneath the ash for 300 million years.

C.why: You chose the event that uncovered the trees. An excavation happens now, so it cannot have been preserved for 300 million years.

D.why: You chose the material that did the preserving. The ash covered the forest, and the ash being "preserved beneath the ash" makes no sense. The trees are what was preserved.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Among the thousands of worlds identified in recent transit surveys, a few gas giants circle so close to their stars that a full year lasts less than a day. One such planet, catalogued by an international team last spring, is an extreme example. Orbiting its host star once every 18 hours, ______. At such temperatures, some metals in its upper atmosphere would exist as vapor.
choices: the planet's surface is likely heated to well over 2,000 degrees Celsius
astronomers estimate that the planet is heated to over 2,000 degrees Celsius
the planet, which astronomers think is heated to over 2,000 degrees Celsius
the planet is likely heated to a temperature of over 2,000 degrees Celsius
explanation: The planet is what orbits the star every 18 hours, so "the planet" has to come right after the comma. Choices C and D both do that, but only D gives "the planet" a main verb, "is heated," which makes it a complete sentence.

A.why: You chose the planet's property instead of the planet itself. "Planet's" is only a possessive, and the subject is "surface." A surface doesn't orbit a star. The whole planet does.

B.why: You chose the people doing the studying. The sentence would say the astronomers orbit the star once every 18 hours.

C.why: You found the right noun but didn't check for a main verb. "Is heated" belongs to the "which" clause, so "the planet" has no verb of its own and the sentence is a fragment.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In the 1990s, linguist Ayla Demir began recording a whistled form of Turkish used by farmers in a few hillside villages near the Black Sea. Because whistles carry much farther than spoken words, farmers on opposite slopes can exchange detailed messages without shouting. Demir's recordings show that the system keeps the stress pattern of every word it imitates. Encoded entirely in shifts of pitch and length rather than in ordinary vowels and consonants, ______
choices: Demir found that the whistled form can still be understood by listeners on distant slopes.
the whistled form can still be understood by trained listeners on distant slopes.
trained listeners on distant slopes can still understand the whistled form.
the pitch of the whistled form can still be understood by listeners on distant slopes.
explanation: Ask what is encoded in shifts of pitch and length. It is the whistled form of the language, so the whistled form has to be the first noun after the comma. Choice B is the only one that puts it there, so the modifier attaches to the right thing.

A.why: You put the researcher where the language belongs. Demir recorded the whistled form, but she is not encoded in shifts of pitch. Starting with her makes the opening phrase describe her.

C.why: You started with the listeners, who are the people affected. The listeners are not encoded in pitch. The language is.

D.why: You chose a property of the language instead of the language itself. 'The pitch of...' makes the pitch the subject, so the sentence says the pitch is encoded in shifts of pitch. That makes no sense.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Agronomists in central Malawi have been testing whether intercropping can reduce farmers' need for purchased fertilizer. In a three-year trial, plots that paired maize with a legume produced yields close to those of plots given a full dose of urea. For most plots, the legume chosen was the cowpea. Planted between the maize rows a few weeks after the main crop emerges, ______
choices: the trial's farmers relied on cowpeas to shade the soil and return nitrogen to it.
the soil is shaded by cowpeas, which return nitrogen to it as their roots decay.
the nitrogen from cowpeas enriches the soil as their roots break down and decay.
cowpeas shade the soil and return nitrogen to it as their roots break down.
explanation: The cowpeas are what is planted between the maize rows, so 'cowpeas' must come right after the comma. Choice D does that. How smooth the other choices sound does not matter here. Only the first noun decides it.

A.why: You started with the farmers, who do the planting. The farmers are not planted between the rows. The modifier needs the crop, not the people tending it.

B.why: You made the soil the subject. The soil is not planted between maize rows. Moving 'cowpeas' into a 'by' phrase pushes the real subject out of first place.

C.why: You started with something the plant produces. Nitrogen is not planted between rows. 'The nitrogen from cowpeas' quietly moves the subject away from the cowpeas themselves.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: A bound volume of lute music held by a Swedish library has long puzzled scholars. Its paper dates to the 1640s, yet some of its pieces imitate styles that did not become fashionable until decades later. Musicologist Henrik Lund argues that the volume grew gradually as successive owners added to it. Copied by at least three different hands over roughly half a century, ______
choices: Lund believes the volume includes dances that appear in no printed collection.
the composers of the volume's dances are absent from every printed collection.
the volume includes dances that appear in no printed collection of the period.
the volume's successive owners included dances absent from printed collections.
explanation: The volume is what was copied by three different hands, so it has to come right after the comma. Choice C opens with 'the volume' and attaches the modifier correctly.

A.why: You started with the scholar who studies the volume. Lund was not copied by three hands. Starting with him makes the opening phrase describe the wrong person.

B.why: You started with the makers of the music. Composers are not copied by hand, so 'the composers of...' moves the subject away from the book.

D.why: You started with the owners, the people who did the work. The owners added pages, but the owners themselves were not copied. The thing that was copied was the volume.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Each autumn, blackpoll warblers leave the forests of northeastern North America for South America. For decades, ornithologists suspected that the birds flew straight over the Atlantic Ocean rather than following the coastline, but the songbirds were too small to carry conventional tracking transmitters. Fitted with geolocators weighing only about half a gram, ______
choices: several warblers confirmed the suspicion, crossing the ocean nonstop in about three days.
ornithologists confirmed the suspicion when warblers crossed the ocean nonstop in three days.
the suspicion was confirmed when warblers crossed the ocean nonstop in about three days.
the flights of several warblers confirmed the suspicion, crossing the ocean in three days.
explanation: The birds wore the geolocators, so 'warblers' has to be the first noun after the comma. Choice A is the only one that starts with the birds themselves.

B.why: You started with the people acting instead of the birds. The ornithologists attached the devices, but nobody fitted the ornithologists with geolocators.

C.why: You made 'the suspicion' the subject. An idea can't wear a tracking device. Putting 'warblers' inside a 'when' clause takes them out of the subject position.

D.why: You started with something the birds did instead of the birds. 'The flights of several warblers' makes the flights the subject, and flights are not fitted with geolocators.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Most jellyfish follow a one-way life cycle: a drifting larva settles, grows into a stalk-like polyp, and buds off free-swimming medusae that eventually die. One small species found in temperate and tropical seas breaks this pattern. Capable of turning back its own development when it is injured or starved, ______
choices: biologists have watched Turritopsis dohrnii revert from a medusa to a young polyp.
the life cycle of Turritopsis dohrnii can run backward from medusa to young polyp.
Turritopsis dohrnii can revert from a mature medusa to a young, stalk-like polyp.
a mature medusa's reversion to a polyp makes Turritopsis dohrnii nearly unique.
explanation: The opening phrase describes the animal, which can turn back its own development when it is injured or starved. Choice C names that species first, so the modifier attaches correctly.

A.why: You started with the observers. Biologists can't turn back their own development. The species can.

B.why: You started with 'the life cycle of...', which moves the subject away from the animal. A life cycle doesn't get injured or starved, and it doesn't have development of its own.

D.why: You started with the process instead of the creature. 'Reversion' is what the jellyfish does, but a reversion can't be injured or starved, so the modifier attaches to the wrong noun.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: During a multiyear tagging study off the coast of southern California, marine biologists compared the foraging dives of bottlenose dolphins with those of Cuvier's beaked whales. The dolphins seldom descended below about 300 meters, staying mostly in sunlit and twilight waters. Plunging roughly 2,700 meters deeper than that on its longest recorded dive, ______ a depth of nearly 3,000 meters and stayed submerged for more than two hours.
choices: the deepest dive of one beaked whale reached
one of the tagged beaked whales reached
the team followed one beaked whale to
one of the tagged beaked whales, reaching
explanation: The opening phrase "Plunging roughly 2,700 meters deeper... on its longest recorded dive" describes an animal, so the first noun after the comma has to be the animal that plunged. "One of the tagged beaked whales" is that animal. The finite verb "reached" also pairs correctly with "and stayed submerged."

A.why: You put the whale's property first instead of the whale. A dive can't plunge "on its longest recorded dive," and a dive can't "stay submerged." The opening phrase describes the whale, not what it did.

C.why: You put the people doing the study first instead of the animal. The researchers didn't plunge 2,700 meters, and they didn't stay submerged for two hours.

D.why: You started with the right noun but swapped the main verb for "reaching." That leaves "whales" without a finite verb, and nothing grammatical comes before "and stayed submerged."

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: A 2019 survey of the construction trades in three Midwestern states compared pay and benefits for two groups of licensed electricians: those who belonged to a union and those who did not. The gap in hourly pay was large. Earning about seven dollars more per hour than their nonunion counterparts with similar experience, ______ were also more likely to receive employer-paid health coverage, the survey's authors reported.
choices: the hourly pay of unionized electricians
unionized electricians in the survey
the unions representing these electricians
employers of unionized electricians
explanation: Ask who earned seven dollars more per hour than "their nonunion counterparts." It was the electricians. "Unionized electricians in the survey" puts them first, right after the comma, and they are also the ones who were more likely to receive health coverage.

C.why: You picked the organization connected to the workers. The unions didn't earn the higher hourly wage. Their members did.

D.why: You picked the people on the other side of the paycheck. Employers pay the wages and provide the coverage. They aren't the ones earning more than nonunion counterparts.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: In a trial of an influenza vaccine for adults over 65, researchers gave one group the standard formulation and a second group a version containing an adjuvant, a compound added to strengthen the body's immune response. Blood samples taken a month later showed a clear difference between the groups. Producing antibody levels about four times higher than those of the standard group, ______ also remained protected for several months longer.
choices: the adjuvant mixed into the vaccine
volunteers given the adjuvanted version
researchers analyzing the blood samples
antibodies from the adjuvanted group
explanation: Antibodies are produced by people's immune systems, so the thing doing the "producing" is the vaccinated people. "Volunteers given the adjuvanted version" puts them right after the comma, and they are also the ones who "remained protected."

A.why: You picked the cause rather than the thing doing the action. The adjuvant boosts the response, but it doesn't produce antibodies, and it can't "remain protected."

C.why: You picked the people who measured the result instead of the people it happened to. The researchers didn't produce the antibodies. They tested the samples.

D.why: You picked what was produced instead of who produced it. Antibodies can't produce "antibody levels," so the opening phrase dangles.

stimulus: In 1907, folklorist Ansgar Moe carried a phonograph through the fjord villages of western Norway. He recorded elderly singers whose tunes had never been written down. A century later, musicologist Ingrid Halvorsen returned to those fragile wax cylinders and listened to them hundreds of times at reduced speed. Notated by hand over six years, ______
choices: Halvorsen restored forty-two melodies that keep the vocal ornaments earlier anthologies had smoothed away.
the forty-two melodies keeps the vocal ornaments that earlier folk anthologies had smoothed away.
the forty-two melodies keep the vocal ornaments that earlier folk anthologies had smoothed away.
Halvorsen's project recovered forty-two melodies that keep the ornaments earlier anthologies had smoothed away.
explanation: Ask what was notated by hand over six years. The melodies were, so the first noun after the comma has to be the melodies. Choice C starts with that noun, and it pairs the plural subject 'melodies' with the plural verb 'keep'.

B.why: You found the right subject and stopped checking. 'Melodies' is plural, so it needs 'keep,' not the singular 'keeps.'

D.why: You chose a related noun, the project, over the thing that was actually notated. A project cannot be written out by hand, and the melodies can.

stimulus: Most color woodcuts use a separate block for each color. Printmaker Odile Ferrant preferred the riskier reduction method. She carved away more of the same block after every color was printed, which meant the earlier stages could never be printed again. the pearwood block bore eleven colors, each of which required realigning the paper by hand.
the river scene having eleven colors, each of which required realigning the paper by hand.
the river scene has eleven colors, each of which required realigning the paper by hand.

district residents now encounter about a third fewer cars and twice as many cyclists.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Twice each day, meteorologists at hundreds of stations around the world release balloons carrying radiosondes, compact instrument packages that measure temperature, humidity, and air pressure. Climbing through the atmosphere at roughly five meters per second, ______ Forecasters then feed these measurements into the computer models that generate the coming week's predictions.
choices: a reading is sent by the radiosonde to a ground station every second.
the radiosonde sends a reading to a ground station every second.
the radiosonde's readings reach a ground station every second.
the radiosonde sending a reading to a ground station every second.
explanation: The opening phrase 'Climbing through the atmosphere at roughly five meters per second' has no subject of its own, so the first noun after the comma must be the thing doing the climbing. That is the radiosonde. Choice B puts 'the radiosonde' first and gives it a finite verb, 'sends', so the sentence is complete.

A.why: You picked a choice whose first noun is 'a reading'. A reading doesn't climb through the atmosphere. The passive voice moves the radiosonde to the end of the clause, so the opening phrase ends up attached to the wrong noun.

C.why: You saw 'radiosonde' first and stopped reading. In 'the radiosonde's readings', the radiosonde is only a possessive, and the grammatical subject is 'readings'. That makes the readings the thing climbing, which is the object-instead-of-its-property trap.

D.why: You found the right subject, but 'sending' is a nonfinite -ing form. The sentence never gets a main verb, so what's left is a fragment.

stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
stimulus: Economists have long debated whether changing employers pays off over the course of a career or merely trades security for a short-term raise. economist Lena Odum found that frequent job switchers out-earned those who stayed.
economist Lena Odum found, that frequent job switchers out-earned those who stayed.

D.why: You got the subject right but missed the punctuation. A comma between 'found' and its object clause 'that frequent job switchers...' cuts a verb off from its object, so it sits at a grammatically incoherent point.

the fossil leaves still display their branching veins and tiny breathing pores.
